A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical parameterization approach to dataset distillation, renamed from H-GLaD to H-PD. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-subset distillation results, architecture-transfer evaluations, timing measurements, ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations on Tiny-ImageNet and full ImageNet-1K, along with comparisons against diffusion-based distillation methods.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains averaged-noise initialization, progressive optimization through GAN feature domains, feature-distance-based latent selection, and final accuracy-based dataset selection. The matching objectives and gradient-based feature-distance formula are unchanged. Renaming H-GLaD to H-PD and evaluating additional distillation backbones do not establish a revised core procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual distillation and evaluation on Tiny-ImageNet and full ImageNet-1K, substantially extending the retained CIFAR-10 and ten-class ImageNet-subset coverage. It removes the explicit tests using Pokemon-pretrained, FFHQ-pretrained, and randomly initialized generators from v1 Appendix B.3.

E2.justification: v3 Table 6 adds evaluated Minimax and D4M comparators on existing ImageNet subsets, while Table 2 introduces SRe2L-based Pixel/GLaD/H-PD comparisons. Retained MTT/DC rows are relabeled TESLA/DSA, often with identical scores and settings; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E3.justification: New experiments use ResNet-18 for SRe2L evaluations at 64×64 and 224×224, with GLaD layer 12 specified. The diffusion comparison explicitly uses 128×128 images and one-hot labels without training-time matching or mixup. These are bounded protocol additions; the retained experiments largely preserve their evaluation design and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The complete generator-pretraining robustness investigation in v1 Table 10 and Appendix B.3 is removed, eliminating a distinct test of dependence on relevant generative priors. Figure 5 also loses its MTT and DC correlation panels, and the component ablation loses its ImageNet-Birds column. Most other sensitivity, initialization, searching-strategy, and CAM analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five evaluation repetitions or five randomly initialized evaluation networks and report results with ± quantities. Neither introduces new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds SRe2L and diffusion-comparison results. For example, Table 2 reports ImageNet-1K IPC=10 accuracy of 23.5±0.4 for H-PD versus 21.9±0.8 for GLaD, without a corresponding v1 experiment. The DM result at 100 steps changes from 6.5±1.4 to 36.5±1.4. Pretraining-study results and five cross-architecture dataset columns are removed; most matched remaining values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.2 adds an expected-cost inequality using mutual information, KL divergence, and conditional entropy, under assumptions about lossless distribution matching and optimized latents. This formal argument is absent from v1. The earlier appendix's qualitative fixed-versus-unfixed optimization discussion is also moved and expanded, but that relocation alone is not new theory.

C1.justification: v3 reframes the contribution as a general hierarchical parameterization framework, with GAN-based distillation as its demonstration, rather than principally an exploration of GAN priors. Its abstract additionally claims superiority over diffusion-based distillation at IPC=1 and IPC=10, and its conclusion emphasizes extreme-compression performance.

C2.justification: v3 argues that diffusion-based generation becomes effectively random sampling or coreset selection under extreme compression. It removes v1's interpretations concerning transfer from unrelated GAN pretraining datasets and the FFHQ feature mismatch. Most explanations involving CAM, DM overfitting, initialization, and layer allocation remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 provides an authors' H-PD code URL, whereas v1 identifies the upstream GLaD implementation. It removes the explicit evaluation schedule of 500 warm-up epochs followed by 500 cosine-decay epochs. Hardware, augmentation details, expert-trajectory information, and the retained hyperparameter values largely carry over.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands substantially to distinguish optimization-based GAN parameterization from diffusion-based distillation, supported by new diffusion, SRe2L, optimal-transport, and GAN-inversion references. Several earlier references disappear. The CAM citation also changes from Grad-CAM to Eigen-CAM despite retention of the gradient-based formula.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around broader parameterization claims. The method and title are renamed, the fixed-space discussion moves from the appendix into Section 3.2, and the experiment sections are reorganized into separate comparison and evaluation discussions.

P2.justification: The document switches to two-column layout throughout. The original framework diagram is removed, while the appendix's fixed-versus-unfixed diagram is redrawn and promoted to Figure 2. New comparison tables are added, existing tables lose columns, and the hyperparameter table is split. Figure 5 becomes a single panel with incorrectly reversed axis labels.

improvement.justification: The new full ImageNet-1K and Tiny-ImageNet evaluations address v1's restriction to ten-class distillation benchmarks, strengthening evidence about broader applicability. Direct diffusion comparisons and an authors' code link also improve assessability. These gains are limited by removal of the prior-robustness study and overextended claims: Table 6 evaluates diffusion methods only at IPC=1, and the conditional argument in Equation 3 does not establish avoidance of local optima. The net improvement is therefore modest.
